authoring_guidance: Write a concise final answer for a traveler, in the voice of a careful travel advisor. Start with the result in one or two natural sentences. Use friendly headings, visible stable Option A/B/C labels, and a compact comparison table or short option paragraphs. Clearly state exact local departure and arrival dates, since Jan 16 and Jan 17 are different travel outcomes. Do not output a field-by-field dump. Avoid the words admitted, conditional, status, search styles, price completeness, source IDs, hashes, UTC, snake_case, machine codes, or internal checker language. Include factual slots in natural sentences rather than repeating labels. Do not prepend phrases such as 'search coverage was' to the coverage slot because it is already a full sentence. Use provider_status and coverage as complete standalone sentences when needed. Use shared_disclosures only for exact equal slot values across selected options and bind those keys to visible stable option identifiers as the Results contract requires; otherwise show each option's facts in its own part. A single-award journey can show travel departure and arrival once when the award schedule is the same, using any supported equality alias provided by v4, but every required disclosure must remain bound. Keep option-specific caveats beside that option, and shared caveats in one brief closing paragraph. Never assert that an admitted journey has no unresolved requirements unless source requirements are genuinely empty; a source price limitation remains unresolved even when an option is admitted. Do not infer a party-total price, current availability, protection, a confirmed cabin on every leg, or bookability. State reported airline codes only as reported airlines. Use exact factual slots and no duplicated units. For each selected journey satisfy the supplied v4 disclosure keys, including cash component keys when present, and use a visible stable identifier. For benchmark or incomplete observations, set part.identifier to a short visible label; use 'Cash price comparison' for the benchmark heading and identifier, never display observation_id. Copy each claim.text literally into the same part's visible prose and use a defined proposition only when its precise meaning is true. Omit gratuitous negative claim declarations and avoid broad eligibility assertions. Keep parts separated by blank lines. During correction, address every failed binding and claim before polishing prose. Preserve the same selected source references unless a documented source-backed reason requires changing them.
